eyebrow: ServiceNow Security & Access Controls · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 10 · Authentication & Single Sign-On

code:
Password alone:                    Password + MFA:
"something you know"                "something you know"
 -- stealable via phishing,            PLUS
    breach, or keylogger              "something you have"
                                        -- a device, a one-time code
A stolen password = full access.    A stolen password alone = nothing.
caption: MFA doesn't stop theft; it defeats what the theft is worth.

eyebrow: MFA mapped onto the SAML flow
code:
1. User navigates to ServiceNow
2. Redirected to the IdP
3. Authenticates AT the IdP --
   password AND one-time code / push approval
4-7. IdP signs assertion -> ServiceNow validates -> logs in
caption: MFA inserts itself into Step 3; ServiceNow's role never changes.

steps.label: One chokepoint
steps.sub: the IdP already sits in front of the whole app portfolio

steps.label: Consistent enforcement
steps.sub: configure once, applies to every connected app

steps.label: Troubleshooting
steps.sub: an MFA failure is usually IdP-side, not a ServiceNow problem
